capital-compute-flow: Flow graph with ten named parties in columns: finance, chip makers, labs, clouds. Capital arrows run from NVIDIA, SoftBank, Amazon and Microsoft into OpenAI and from NVIDIA and Microsoft into Anthropic; NVIDIA puts 2 billion dollars into CoreWeave; Blue Owl funds put 7 billion dollars cash into a Meta venture. Dashed arrows show purchase commitments from OpenAI and Meta to CoreWeave and a warrant from AMD to OpenAI. Text lists the larger commitments of OpenAI to Microsoft and Amazon.
capex-vs-cash-flow: Six small bar charts of annual capital spending and operating cash flow for Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle and CoreWeave. Spending rises sharply in all six. Capital spending stays below operating cash flow for Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta, nearly equals it for Amazon in 2025, and exceeds it for Oracle in fiscal 2025 and 2026 and for CoreWeave in every year.
closed-loop-bounds: Three horizontal bars. NVIDIA alone supplied up to 24.6 percent of OpenAI March 2026 round. NVIDIA plus Amazon at its stated maximum is up to 65.6 percent. Documented NVIDIA capital to customers is at most 19.5 percent of its fiscal 2026 revenue.
customer-concentration: Horizontal bars of disclosed customer shares: NVIDIA two direct customers at 22 and 14 percent; CoreWeave Microsoft 67 percent in 2025, top two 77 percent in 2024, top three 73 percent in 2023.
commitments-vs-revenue: Log-scale bars. OpenAI 2025 revenue 13.1 billion dollars against contracted purchases of 250 billion dollars from Microsoft Azure and 38 billion dollars from AWS. CoreWeave revenue 5.1 billion against 60.7 billion obligations. Oracle revenue 67.4 billion against 664 billion obligations.
depreciation-lives: Dot and arrow chart of stated server lives in years. CoreWeave lengthened from 5 to 6 in 2023, Amazon shortened a subset from 6 to 5 in 2025, Meta set 5.5 in 2025, Alphabet uses 6, Microsoft states 2 to 6 and Oracle 1 to 6.
hyperion-structure: Diagram: Meta holds 20 percent and Blue Owl funds 80 percent of a joint venture that owns a Louisiana data center campus. Blue Owl paid 7 billion dollars cash at closing; Meta contributed 4.3 billion dollars of assets and received a 2.6 billion dollar distribution.
hardware-efficiency: Scatter on a log axis of peak tensor operations per watt for twelve accelerators from 2016 to 2024 with a dashed fit of about 1.4 times per year.
accelerator-hour-cost: Horizontal stacked bars of cost per utilized accelerator-hour for lives of 5 and 6 years and utilization of 40, 60 and 80 percent. Capital dominates; electricity is a thin slice. Cost ranges from about 0.96 to 2.2 dollars per hour.
price-decomposition: Three log-scale bars: hardware cost decline explains about 2 times, hardware energy efficiency about 1.9 times, against an observed 280 times price fall; the remaining factor is about 141 times.
open-compute-lag: Dumbbell chart for training-compute thresholds from 1e22 to 1e26 FLOP: the first notable model at any access type and the first open-weight model, with the gap in months shrinking from about 30 months at 1e23 to 15 months at 1e25 and no open-weight model yet at 1e26 in the data.
research-to-product-lag: Three dumbbells showing months between a method paper and a shipped system: FlashAttention to PyTorch 2.0 about 10 months, Mamba to Jamba about 3 months, speculative decoding to Google products about 24 months.
alternative-hardware-ratios: Horizontal bars of ratios against a baseline: BitNet on CPU energy 6.6 to 23.2 times lower by estimate, memory 3.5 to 12 times lower, FlightLLM FPGA 4.2 to 6.0 times energy efficiency and 1.4 to 1.8 times cost efficiency versus two GPUs, Loihi 2 about 2 times less energy preliminary.
map-frontier-datacenters: World map with red circles sized by frontier AI data-center power: United States about 11.9 gigawatts, Malaysia 1.1, China 0.7, and small sites in the United Kingdom, Finland, Indonesia, Norway, Australia, Portugal and Iceland.
map-notable-models: World map shading countries by notable AI models released in 2025: United States 59, China 35, South Korea 8, and one each for Canada, France, Singapore and the United Kingdom.
map-national-programs: World map with callouts for national compute programs: Brazil R$ 23.03 billion plan, EU 200 billion euro InvestAI goal with a 20 billion euro gigafactory fund, Saudi Arabia up to 500 MW, UAE 1 GW Stargate, India 38,231 GPUs, China 1.59 million PFLOPS, South Korea 260,000 GPUs, Japan at least 10 trillion yen to FY2030, United States 11.9 GW of listed frontier sites.
adoption-by-country: Horizontal bars of the share of firms using AI in official surveys: South Korea 32.9, Germany 26, Spain 21.1, EU 20.0, United States 18, OECD 13.9, Brazil 13, France 10 percent.
timeline-capability-vs-deployment: Two-lane timeline from 2022 to 2026 with numbered markers and a legend. Upper lane lists method and model releases such as Chinchilla, FlashAttention, speculative decoding, Mamba, DeepSeek-V3 and R1, native sparse attention and BitNet. Lower lane lists deployments and financing events from PyTorch 2.0 in March 2023 to the OpenAI 122 billion dollar round in March 2026.
cadence-vs-quarter: Timeline of quarterly decision dates with three example readiness times and the weeks each waits until the next date; text states the average wait is half the period.
forcing-function-threshold: A decreasing curve of gain against outside cost with two dashed horizontal levels: a high gate level before a tool and a low level after it. The curve crosses the low level earlier as cost falls.
small-multiples: Four small bar panels: capital per H100-equivalent across 74 sites, facility watts per H100-equivalent, peak tensor efficiency of twelve accelerators in release order, and listed power in the six largest countries.
